{"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-007","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"material","page":1,"quote":"Polyurethene"},{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"HARDENED 40-45 HRC"}],"comment":"The title block specifies material as polyurethane but also calls for hardening to 40-45 HRC, a heat treatment and hardness scale that cannot be applied to a polymer. The designer must correct either the material or remove the impossible heat treatment specification."
    ,
"recommended_correction":"Remove the heat treatment callout if the part is polyurethane, or change the material field if a hardenable metal was intended."},{"rule_id":"MF-007","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"material","page":1,"quote":"Polyurethene"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N2","page":1,"quote":"SHORE HARDNESS- 80±5"}],"comment":"Note N2 specifies Shore hardness, which is appropriate for the stated polyurethane material, directly conflicting with the title block's Rockwell C (HRC) hardness callout in the heat_treatment field. This contradiction will confuse manufacturing about which hardness standard applies."
    ,
"recommended_correction":"Remove the 'HARDENED 40-45 HRC' from the heat_treatment field so that only the Shore hardness note governs the polyurethane part."}]}
